name: vault-browse-away
comment: Vault Browse face execution plan, Slice 6 (living tile states) — the design's signature 'nothing disappears' contract (§4.7): a confirmed root whose directory does not exist on disk at boot, with a durably published index for it built directly (tests/fixtures/vault/browse-states-away-seed/vault/index-v1.sqlite, hand-built against VaultIndex's own schema — the fixture is not reachable by a live scan since it never existed on disk; the seed IS the 'the root was scanned once, then the drive was pulled' state VaultWatcher::refresh() finds at boot). Ground-truth finding recorded here: VaultKit::planBrowseLevel structurally cannot walk a vanished directory, so decorating an empty node list satisfies nothing — VaultLibrary::browseAt() falls back to VaultBrowseAway::offlineBrowseAt() (new this slice), which is what this scenario actually proves end to end. Run with --seed tests/fixtures/vault/browse-states-away-seed.

steps.label: the session answers, drive gated on
one visible window, isolated data root
the boot splash has left the screen
open the Vault via the folder door
the vault paints populated even though its only root is gone
the rail marks the root unavailable (VaultWatcher::refresh() noticing the vanished drive at boot)
THE CONTRACT: the grid still shows both tiles the index remembers — not zero (offlineBrowseAt fallback)
the single-file group reads as a film tile, marked away, unopenable
the two-file group folds to a plain folder tile, also away
visual evidence: the away grid — tiles present, marked away, nothing missing
